title: Pricing a Bench Estimate from the Level Schedule
content:
# Costing Note: Pricing a Bench Estimate from the Level Schedule

This note sets out how the bench of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service arrives at the figure on an estimate, and how long that figure stands.

## What a priced line comes to

The bench prices the work from the level's own schedule: labour at the level's hourly bench rate with a floor at the level's minimum labour charge, and each named task at the charge the level lists for it. A priced line is the unit price of the task multiplied by the number of units, rounded to the nearest cent, and never less than the level's minimum labour charge; where the multiplied figure falls below that floor, the floor is what the line comes to.

Stone setting is priced from the level's carat ladder by the weight of the stone set, and the band a stone falls in is decided by its recorded weight rather than by its appearance.

Bench labour carries the level's metal surcharge for the metal the piece is confirmed to be in at intake, and the surcharge is applied to labour alone and never to parts.

## The estimate itself

An estimate is prepared without charge at the levels that offer it free, and where a charge applies it is credited against the work at the levels that credit it and kept where they do not. An estimate charge is booked to the order as its own priced line under the estimate charge code, so it can be told apart from the bench work it may later be credited against.

An estimate stays good for the level's validity window, and once it has run out the piece is repriced rather than worked to the old figure.

## When an estimate may be put to the customer

An estimate is put to the customer only while the order stands at estimated or already awaiting authorization. The state the order stands at is read from the work order record, correlated by its work order reference, before the estimate is put.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Take a hypothetical order at a level whose minimum labour charge is 95.00 USD and whose hourly bench rate is 185.00 USD. A task priced at 0.25 hours of jeweler time comes to 46.25 USD before the floor; below the level's minimum labour charge, the line comes to 95.00 USD. A task of 2 hours comes to 370.00 USD, above the floor, so the line stands at 370.00 USD. Were that piece confirmed at intake to be in a metal carrying a surcharge of 10 percent, the surcharge on the second line would be 37.00 USD, and a part fitted alongside it would carry no surcharge at all.

## Points of judgement

| The records show | The estimate may be put to the customer |
|---|---|
| The order stands at estimated | yes |
| The order stands at awaiting authorization | yes |
| The order stands at intake | no |
| The order stands in workshop | no |
